## Motivation

On CUDA, `ggml_mul_mat_a8` is the dp4a MMQ that vLLM copied from llama.cpp in 2024 (b2899). Since then llama.cpp's MMQ has moved to int8 tensor-core `mma` instructions, stream-k scheduling and kernels for the i-quants. At prefill sizes, SGLang's GGUF linear layers are now **8-15x slower** than llama.cpp on the same GPU. The i-quants (IQ2_*, IQ3_*, IQ4_*, IQ1_S) have no MMQ at all here: they dequantize the whole weight to bf16 on every call.

Low-bit GGUF releases of large MoE models are now common: IQ2/IQ3/IQ4 experts, with Q4_K/Q6_K dense layers. This PR replaces the CUDA implementation behind `ggml_mul_mat_a8` with llama.cpp's current MMQ and extends MMQ to all GGUF weight types except IQ1_M.

All numbers below are from an RTX 5070 Ti (sm_120) with bf16 activations. The table is ms per call, for an 11008 x 4096 weight streamed from DRAM, timed as 20 calls in a CUDA graph:

| type | M | main (dp4a MMQ, or dequant for IQ) | **this PR** | dequant + bf16 GEMM | llama.cpp (test-backend-ops) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q4_K | 256 / 4096 / 16384 | 2.41 / 38.4 / 154 | **0.193 / 3.10 / 13.9** | 0.380 / 4.02 / 15.5 | 0.182 / 2.82 / 12.8 |
| Q6_K | 256 / 4096 / 16384 | 3.11 / 49.4 / 198 | **0.261 / 3.88 / 17.1** | 0.393 / 4.03 / 15.5 | 0.256 / 3.60 / 15.9 |
| Q8_0 | 256 / 4096 | 2.38 / 37.9 | **0.207 / 2.90** | 0.423 / 4.07 | 0.205 / 2.64 |
| Q2_K | 256 / 4096 | 1.48 / 24.1 | **0.314 / 4.68** | 0.371 / 4.01 | 0.305 / 4.38 |
| IQ4_XS | 16 / 256 / 4096 | dequant: 0.246 / 0.382 / 4.02 | **0.039 / 0.173 / 2.85** | (same as main) | 0.030 / 0.167 / 2.59 |
| IQ3_S | 16 / 256 / 4096 | dequant: 0.245 / 0.385 / 4.03 | **0.052 / 0.189 / 3.10** | (same as main) | 0.041 / 0.182 / 2.83 |

## Modifications

### Vendored llama.cpp
`python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/quantization/gguf/llama_mmq/ggml/` holds llama.cpp commit `23b0202a189c44a54625aadcb37a946dd1d6278d`, verbatim; the one change to it is kept as a patch file applied at build time (see *bf16 / fp16 output* below):
- MMQ headers and template instances, `mma.cuh`, `vecdotq.cuh`, `quantize.cuh`, `common.cuh`, `ggml-common.h`, and the ggml headers they include
- 45 files, about 18.5K lines, **unmodified**
- `SHA256SUMS` and the upstream LICENSE (MIT) sit next to them, and `THIRDPARTYNOTICES.txt` carries the notice

The shim and entry points around them:
- **`llama_mmq/ggml_shim.cu`** (139 lines) supplies what the vendored code links against:
  - `ggml_cuda_info()`, built from `cudaDeviceProp`
  - a pool backed by `c10::cuda::CUDACachingAllocator` (`raw_alloc_with_stream`), which is safe under graph capture
  - errors as `std::runtime_error`
- **`llama_mmq/mmq_dense.cu`** (198 lines) is the 2D path of llama.cpp's `ggml_cuda_mul_mat_q`: tile selection, `GGML_PREC_Q8` and `mul_mat_q_case<type>`.
- **`llama_mmq/quantize_mmq_q8_1.cu`** (197 lines) is llama.cpp's `quantize_mmq_q8_1`, templated to read fp32/fp16/bf16 directly, so bf16 activations need no conversion pass.
  - Block sums are taken over the quantized values, as in #43636.
  - The file carries an MIT attribution.
- **`llama_mmq/sgl_llama_mmq.h`** is the boundary between torch and ggml; neither header includes the other.

### bf16 / fp16 output (second commit)
llama.cpp's MMQ writes fp32; SGLang's activations are bf16. Instead of an fp32 output plus a cast (an extra round trip over the output and an fp32 temporary of M x N, e.g. 721 MB at M = 16384 for an 11008-row weight), the kernel writes X's dtype directly:
- `llama_mmq/patches/0001-mmq-dst-type.patch` (+61 lines in `mmq.cuh`) adds a runtime destination type to `mmq_args` (no extra template instances). CMake copies the vendored `ggml/` into the build tree and applies the patch there, so the tree in the repository stays verbatim (`sha256sum -c ggml/SHA256SUMS` passes) and a re-vendor that no longer applies fails loudly.
- Stream-k: a block that finishes a tile another block started would round twice if its partial sums went through the half-precision output, so partial sums stay fp32 in the fixup buffer and are rounded once.
- Results are bit-identical to the fp32 result rounded to bf16 / fp16 (912 cases: all 18 types x 2 shapes x M = 2..2050, and 5 types x 2 large shapes up to M = 16384).

### `gguf_kernel.cu`
- `ggml_mul_mat_a8` keeps its schema and output dtype.
- On CUDA it calls the new MMQ, which writes X's dtype directly (see above).
- MUSA keeps the dp4a kernel (`#ifdef USE_MUSA`).
- An unsupported type now raises (`TORCH_CHECK`). The old kernel silently returned an uninitialized tensor for i-quants.

### `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/gguf.py`
- `MMQ_QUANT_TYPES` on CUDA covers all standard, K and i-quant types except IQ1_M (Q8_1 is an activation format). MUSA keeps standard + K.
- `MOE_MMQ_QUANT_TYPES` (standard + K) gates `fused_moe_gguf`'s MMQ branch, because the MoE kernel is still the dp4a one (see Follow-ups).
- `fused_mul_mat_gguf`: for CUDA MMQ types, MMVQ is used for a single token only.
  - I measured 10 types x 4 shapes. MMVQ wins only at M=1 (by up to 1.8x); MMQ is faster from M=2. At M=16, MMVQ is 2.5-11x slower.
  - The old cutoffs (2/6, and 8/16 for i-quants) were tuned against the dp4a MMQ and the dequant path.
- **Padding.** llama.cpp's MMQ reads each weight row in steps of 256 values. When K % 512 != 0 it reads past the last row, which is why ggml pads its tensors to a multiple of 512 values (`MATRIX_ROW_PADDING`). This PR pads the same way, with zeros:
  - Unmerged weights are padded once at load.
  - Merged QKV and gate/up shards keep main's layout; `_gguf_mmq_shard` passes a shard as a view when the bytes after it suffice, and otherwise makes the one per-forward copy main already makes, into a buffer that ends with the zero padding. That is never more copies than main, and the same number when K % 512 == 0.
  - The op itself still pads an unpadded weight with a per-call copy (warning once), so other callers stay correct.

### Build (`CMakeLists.txt`)
- An OBJECT library `sgl_llama_mmq` with its own include path is linked into both common_ops libraries. No ggml symbols are exported.
- It is compiled for **sm_80, sm_90, sm_100f and sm_120a**. The sm_80 SASS runs on 8.x, and all 8.x share the same Ampere tile config.
- Objects total about 35.7 MB with `--compress-mode=size` (33.9 MB before the bf16 / fp16 output, +2.3 MB), and take about 80 s with 32 jobs.
- The bf16 / fp16 output patch is applied by CMake to a copy of the vendored tree in the build directory, so `patch` must be available at configure time.
- `.pre-commit-config.yaml` excludes the vendored directory, because codespell flags an upstream spelling.

## Accuracy Tests

`python/sglang/kernels/aot/tests/test_gguf.py` gains the following MMQ coverage:
- **All sample types**, including the i-quants, at 7, 8, 9, 65, 128, 129 and 2050 tokens.
- **Synthetic weights for 18 types**:
  - rows = 1000 with K = 2304, which hits the fallback tiles and the tail
  - 1024 x 2048
  - bf16, fp16 and fp32 activations
  - padded vs unpadded weights, which must be bit-identical
  - strided X
- M = 16384 for three types.
- Unsupported types must raise.
- CUDA graph capture and replay.

Relative L2 against gguf-py's dequantization is 5.3e-3 to 6.1e-3 for every type, which is the q8_1 activation rounding. **235 tests pass** on the first commit and **273** with the second (38 more for the bf16 / fp16 output: bit-exactness against the fp32 result rounded, stream-k fixup shapes, CUDA graph replay), both in a standalone build of the kernels and in the real CMake-built `common_ops` (sm90 library) loaded through `torch.ops`. compute-sanitizer memcheck over the 18 types reports no errors.

Not run: MUSA (not built), and execution on sm_80/90/100 (compile-checked only; execution was on sm_120).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

See the table above (first commit, fp32 output plus cast). Writing bf16 directly (second commit) removes the cast. 11008 x 4096, bf16, ms, first commit -> second commit:

| type | M = 4096 | M = 16384 |
|---|---|---|
| Q4_K | 3.123 -> 2.840 (-9.1%) | 14.075 -> 12.712 (-9.7%) |
| Q6_K | 3.926 -> 3.552 (-9.5%) | 17.372 -> 15.507 (-10.7%) |
| IQ4_XS | 2.884 -> 2.599 (-9.9%) | 12.858 -> 11.447 (-11.0%) |

With this, the port is within a few percent of llama.cpp itself (e.g. Q4_K at M = 16384: 12.71 vs 12.8 ms).

## Dependencies

This branch is stacked on **#43636** (its first two commits: the IQ3_S codebook and the q8_1 block sums). Without #43636 the new IQ3_S tests would fail on main's IQ3_S tables.

This PR does not change the merged-shard layout, which **#43430** handles separately. If #43430 lands first, the padding moves to the end of its flat buffer, a few lines.

## Follow-ups (planned, not in this PR)

1. **MoE with the same MMQ (MUL_MAT_ID).** On main today the GGUF MoE path is slow, and at prefill sizes it breaks. Each row is one MoE layer, in ms at 256 / 1024 / 2560 / 8192 tokens (64 experts, 8 per token, hidden 2560):

   | layer | `fused_moe_gguf` today | llama.cpp MMQ (gate + up + down) |
   |---|---|---|
   | IQ3_S gate/up + IQ4_NL down (I 640) | 8.23 / 33.1 / 82.8 / crashes ("invalid argument") | 0.83 / 1.51 / 3.42 / 10.4 |
   | Q4_K (I 768) | 2.62 / 9.85 / 24.6 / 78.4 (with #43445; main fails above 64 tokens) | 0.93 / 1.67 / 3.68 / 11.4 |
   | Q6_K (I 768) | 3.50 / 13.3 / 33.1 / 106 | 1.17 / 2.05 / 4.43 / 13.4 |

   The plan:
   - A new op `ggml_moe_mmq(X, W, topk_ids, type, row)` that uses llama.cpp's `mm_ids_helper` to route tokens to experts without a host sync.
   - The scatter quantizer, so each token is quantized once for all its top-k.
   - Rewire `fused_moe_gguf` onto it, and drop `moe_align_block_size` for GGUF.
   - About 180 more vendored lines (`mmid.cu`) plus about 300 of entry and dispatch, with MoE tests (there are none today).
2. **Binary size.** If 34 MB per library is too much, the options are:
   - drop sm_80
   - restrict the tile widths to {8, 16, 32, 64, 128}, about 3x smaller but up to 2x wasted compute for 33-127 tokens
   - move the kernels to the JIT path under `python/sglang/kernels/jit`
3. **Q2_K, Q3_K, Q6_K, IQ2_XS and IQ2_S at large M.** These are slower than the other types, and Q2_K / Q6_K / IQ2_S are slower than dequant + bf16 GEMM at large M (Q2_K 18.7 vs 15.5 ms at M = 16384). The same holds in llama.cpp's own kernels: all five carry one scale per 16 values, so the mma path issues two `m16n8k16` per 32 values where the other types issue one `m16n8k32`, and on sm_120 a k16 mma costs the same tensor time as a k32 (measured 49.7 G mma/s for both). For Q2_K and Q3_K the scale can be folded into the int8 weights exactly, which on our side made them 17-28% faster with llama.cpp's tests passing; for Q6_K and IQ2 the product does not fit int8. Such a change belongs in llama.cpp itself, and the vendored copy would pick it up on the next resync. A per-type switch to the dequant path (as in #43626) is possible meanwhile if wanted.

Such a change belongs in llama.cpp itself, and the vendored copy would pick it up on the next resync. A per-type switch to the dequant path (as in #43626) is possible meanwhile if wanted.

+# llama.cpp's int8 tensor-core MMQ kernels behind ggml_mul_mat_a8, vendored under
+# csrc/quantization/gguf/llama_mmq/ggml (see LLAMA_CPP_COMMIT there; MIT). Built once and
+# linked into both common_ops libraries:
+#   * own include paths: the vendored ggml headers define the same block structs as
+#     csrc/quantization/gguf/ggml-common.h, the two only meet through llama_mmq/sgl_llama_mmq.h;
+#   * whole-program device code (no -rdc) and hidden host symbols, so nothing of ggml can
+#     collide with other sources or other libraries in the process;
+#   * -use_fast_math as in llama.cpp's own build;
+#   * SASS for one architecture per family only: sm_80 code runs on sm_86/87/89 and these
+#     kernels take the same code path there (the Ampere config), sm_90 code runs on sm_90a;
+#   * the vendored tree stays byte-identical to llama.cpp: SGLang's changes are the patches in
+#     llama_mmq/patches, applied in order to a copy of ggml/ in the build tree, which is what
+#     gets compiled. The copy is remade when a vendored file or a patch changes.

+foreach(_f IN LISTS SGL_LLAMA_MMQ_VENDORED SGL_LLAMA_MMQ_PATCHES)

+    file(RELATIVE_PATH _r "${SGL_LLAMA_MMQ_DIR}" "${_f}")
+    string(APPEND _sgl_llama_mmq_stamp "${_h}  ${_r}\n")
+endforeach()
+set(_sgl_llama_mmq_stamp_file "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/llama_mmq/inputs.sha256")
+set(_sgl_llama_mmq_old_stamp "")
+if(EXISTS "${_sgl_llama_mmq_stamp_file}")

+endif()
+if(NOT _sgl_llama_mmq_old_stamp STREQUAL _sgl_llama_mmq_stamp OR NOT EXISTS "${SGL_LLAMA_MMQ_GGML}")

+template <typename T> struct block_reduce_policy<block_reduce_method::SUM, T> {
+    static __device__ T reduce(T val) {

+            return make_float2(0.0f, 0.0f);
+        } else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<T, half2>) {
+            return make_half2(0.0f, 0.0f);
+        } else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<T, int>) {

+template <block_reduce_method reduce_method_t, const unsigned int block_size_template = 0, typename T>
+static __device__ T block_reduce(T val, [[maybe_unused]] T * shared_vals) {
+    // for multi-warp reductions, callers must not reuse shared_vals until all reads from this invocation have completed
+    val                           = block_reduce_policy<reduce_method_t, T>::reduce(val);
+    const unsigned int block_size = block_size_template == 0 ? blockDim.x : block_size_template;
+    if (block_size > WARP_SIZE) {
+        assert((block_size <= 1024) && (block_size % WARP_SIZE) == 0);
+        const int warp_id = threadIdx.x / WARP_SIZE;
+        const int lane_id = threadIdx.x % WARP_SIZE;
+        if (lane_id == 0) {
+            shared_vals[warp_id] = val;

+        __syncthreads();

+        }

+    }

+// Aligned memory transfers of 8/16 bytes can be faster than 2 transfers with 4 bytes, especially on AMD.
+// Important: do not use this function if dst and src both point at registers.
+//     Due to the strict aliasing rule the compiler can do incorrect optimizations if src and dst have different types.
+//     The function is intended for copies between registers and SRAM/VRAM to make the compiler emit the right instructions.
+//     If dst and src point at different address spaces then they are guaranteed to not be aliased.
+template <int nbytes, int alignment = 0>
+static __device__ __forceinline__ void ggml_cuda_memcpy_1(void * __restrict__ dst, const void * __restrict__ src) {
+    static_assert(
+        nbytes <= ggml_cuda_get_max_cpy_bytes() || alignment == 0,
+        "You are misusing the alignment parameter for ggml_cuda_memcpy_1. "
+        "The intent is for the parameter is only as a workaround if either one of the pointers is not properly aligned. "
+        "If you use it to do more bytes per copy than ggml_cuda_max_cpy_bytes() the reads and writes may not be coalesced. "
+        "Call ggml_cuda_memcpy_1 in a loop instead.");
+    if constexpr (alignment != 0) {
+        static_assert(nbytes % alignment == 0, "bad alignment");
+    }
+    constexpr int nb_per_cpy = alignment == 0 ? nbytes : alignment;
+
+#pragma unroll
+    for (int i = 0; i < nbytes/nb_per_cpy; ++i) {
+        if constexpr (nb_per_cpy == 1) {
+            ((char *) dst)[i] = ((const char *) src)[i];
+        } else if constexpr (nb_per_cpy == 2) {
+            ((short *) dst)[i] = ((const short *) src)[i];
+        } else if constexpr (nb_per_cpy == 4) {
+            ((int *) dst)[i] = ((const int *) src)[i];
+        } else if constexpr (nb_per_cpy == 8) {
+            ((int2 *) dst)[i] = ((const int2 *) src)[i];
+        } else if constexpr (nb_per_cpy == 16) {
+            ((int4 *) dst)[i] = ((const int4 *) src)[i];
+        } else {
+            static_assert(nbytes == 0 && nbytes == -1, "bad nbytes");
+        }
+    }

+static __device__ __forceinline__ float ggml_cuda_ue4m3_to_fp32(uint8_t x) {
+#if defined(GGML_USE_HIP) && defined(CDNA3) && defined(FP8_AVAILABLE) && HIP_VERSION >= 60200000
+    // ROCm does not support fp8 in software on devices with fp8 hardware,
+    // but CDNA3 supports only e4m3_fnuz (no inf).
+    const uint32_t bits = x * (x != 0x7F && x != 0xFF); // Convert NaN to 0.0f to match CPU implementation.
+    const __hip_fp8_e4m3_fnuz xf = *reinterpret_cast<const __hip_fp8_e4m3_fnuz *>(&bits);
+    return static_cast<float>(xf) / 2;
+#else
+#if defined(FP8_AVAILABLE) && !defined(GGML_USE_HIP)
+    const uint32_t bits = x * (x != 0x7F && x != 0xFF); // Convert NaN to 0.0f to match CPU implementation.
+    const __nv_fp8_e4m3 xf = *reinterpret_cast<const __nv_fp8_e4m3 *>(&bits);
+    return static_cast<float>(xf) / 2;
+#else
+    if (x == 0 || (x == 0x7F && x != 0xFF)) { // Convert NaN to 0.0f
+        return 0.0f;
+    }
+    const int exp = (x >> 3) & 0xF;
+    const int man = x & 0x7;
+    float raw;
+    if (exp == 0) {
+        raw = ldexpf((float) man, -9);
+    } else {
+        raw = ldexpf(1.0f + (float) man / 8.0f, exp - 7);
+    }
+    return static_cast<float>(raw / 2);
+#endif // defined(FP8_AVAILABLE) && !defined(GGML_USE_HIP)
+#endif // defined(GGML_USE_HIP) && defined(CDNA3) && defined(FP8_AVAILABLE) && HIP_VERSION >= 60200000

+__device__ __forceinline__ uint8_t ggml_cuda_float_to_fp4_e2m1(float x, float e) {
+    const uint8_t sign_bit = (x < 0.0f) << 3;
+    float         ax       = fabsf(x) * e;
+
+    // Positive LUT
+    static constexpr float pos_lut[8] = { 0.0f, 0.5f, 1.0f, 1.5f, 2.0f, 3.0f, 4.0f, 6.0f };
+
+    int   best_i   = 0;
+    float best_err = fabsf(ax - pos_lut[0]);
+
+#pragma unroll
+    for (int i = 1; i < 8; ++i) {
+        const float err = fabsf(ax - pos_lut[i]);
+        if (err < best_err) {
+            best_err = err;
+            best_i   = i;
+        }
+    }
+
+    return static_cast<uint8_t>(best_i | sign_bit);
+}

+// See https://gmplib.org/~tege/divcnst-pldi94.pdf figure 4.1.
+// Precompute mp (m' in the paper) and L such that division
+// can be computed using a multiply (high 32b of 64b result)
+// and a shift:
+//
+// n/d = (mulhi(n, mp) + n) >> L;
+static const uint3 init_fastdiv_values(uint64_t d_64) {
+    GGML_ASSERT(d_64 != 0);
+    GGML_ASSERT(d_64 <= std::numeric_limits<uint32_t>::max());
+
+    uint32_t d = (uint32_t)d_64;
+
+    // compute L = ceil(log2(d));
+    uint32_t L = 0;
+    while (L < 32 && (uint32_t{ 1 } << L) < d) {
+        L++;
+    }
+
+    uint32_t mp = (uint32_t) ((uint64_t{ 1 } << 32) * ((uint64_t{ 1 } << L) - d) / d + 1);
+    // pack divisor as well to reduce error surface
+    return make_uint3(mp, L, d);
+}
+
+static __device__ __forceinline__ uint32_t fastdiv(uint32_t n, const uint3 fastdiv_values) {
+    // expects fastdiv_values to contain <mp, L, divisor> in <x, y, z>
+    // fastdiv_values.z is unused and optimized away by the compiler.
+    // Compute high 32 bits of n * mp
+    const uint32_t hi = __umulhi(n, fastdiv_values.x);
+    // add n, apply bit shift
+    return (hi + n) >> fastdiv_values.y;
+}
+
+static __device__ __forceinline__ uint32_t fastmodulo(uint32_t n, const uint3 fastdiv_values) {
+    // expects  fastdiv_values to contain <mp, L, divisor> in <x, y, z> (see init_fastdiv_values)
+    return n - fastdiv(n, fastdiv_values) * fastdiv_values.z;
+}
+
+// Calculate both division and modulo at once, returns <n/divisor, n%divisor>
+static __device__ __forceinline__ uint2 fast_div_modulo(uint32_t n, const uint3 fastdiv_values) {
+    // expects  fastdiv_values to contain <mp, L, divisor> in <x, y, z> (see init_fastdiv_values)
+    const uint32_t div_val = fastdiv(n, fastdiv_values);
+    const uint32_t mod_val = n - div_val * fastdiv_values.z;
+    return make_uint2(div_val, mod_val);
+}

+typedef void (*dequantize_kernel_t)(const void * vx, const int64_t ib, const int iqs, float2 & v);

+using dequantize_kq_t = void (*)(const void * vx, const int64_t ib, dst_t * y, const int tid);

+static __device__ __forceinline__ float get_alibi_slope(
+    const float max_bias, const uint32_t h, const uint32_t n_head_log2, const float m0, const float m1
+) {
+    if (max_bias <= 0.0f) {
+        return 1.0f;
+    }
+    const float base = h < n_head_log2 ? m0 : m1;
+    const int   exph = h < n_head_log2 ? h + 1 : 2*(h - n_head_log2) + 1;
+
+    return powf(base, exph);
+}

+struct ggml_cuda_concurrent_event {
+    std::vector<cudaEvent_t> join_events;
+    cudaEvent_t              fork_event = nullptr;
+
+    int                                          n_streams = 0;
+    std::unordered_map<const ggml_tensor *, int> stream_mapping;
+
+    // Original order of nodes in this concurrent region (before interleaving)
+    // Used to restore grouping for fusion within streams
+    std::vector<const ggml_tensor *> original_order;
+
+    const ggml_tensor * join_node;
+
+    ggml_cuda_concurrent_event() = default;
+
+    ggml_cuda_concurrent_event(const ggml_cuda_concurrent_event &) = delete;
+    ggml_cuda_concurrent_event & operator=(const ggml_cuda_concurrent_event &) = delete;
+
+    explicit ggml_cuda_concurrent_event(int n_streams) : n_streams(n_streams) {
+        join_events.resize(n_streams);
+
+        for (size_t i = 0; i < join_events.size(); ++i) {
+            CUDA_CHECK(cudaEventCreateWithFlags(&join_events[i], cudaEventDisableTiming));
+        }
+
+        CUDA_CHECK(cudaEventCreateWithFlags(&fork_event, cudaEventDisableTiming));
+    }
+
+    ggml_cuda_concurrent_event(ggml_cuda_concurrent_event && other) noexcept
+    : join_events(std::move(other.join_events))
+    , fork_event(other.fork_event)
+    , n_streams(other.n_streams)
+    , stream_mapping(std::move(other.stream_mapping))
+    , original_order(std::move(other.original_order))
+    , join_node(other.join_node) {
+        other.fork_event = nullptr;
+    }
+
+    // 1. check if any branches write to overlapping memory ranges (except the join node)
+    // 2. check whether all srcs are either within the branch or outside the nodes covered by ggml_cuda_concurrent_event
+    // we assume all nodes have the same buffer
+    bool is_valid() const {
+        std::vector<std::vector<std::pair<int64_t, int64_t>>> write_ranges;
+        write_ranges.resize(n_streams);
+
+        // get join_node's memory range to exclude from overlap checking.
+        // multiple nodes can use join_node's buffer; we synchronize on the join node.
+        const ggml_tensor * join_t     = join_node->view_src ? join_node->view_src : join_node;
+        const int64_t       join_start = (int64_t) join_t->data;
+        const int64_t       join_end   = join_start + ggml_nbytes(join_t);
+
+        for (const auto & [tensor, stream] : stream_mapping) {
+            const ggml_tensor * t = tensor->view_src ? tensor->view_src : tensor;
+            const int64_t       t_start = (int64_t) t->data;
+            const int64_t       t_end   = t_start + ggml_nbytes(t);
+
+            // skip tensors that overlap with join_node's buffer.
+            if ((t_start <= join_start && join_start < t_end) || (join_start <= t_start && t_start < join_end)) {
+                continue;
+            }
+
+            // concurrent streams begin from 1
+            write_ranges[stream - 1].emplace_back(t_start, t_end);
+        }
+
+        for (int i = 0; i < n_streams; ++i) {
+            // sorts first by start then by end of write range
+            std::sort(write_ranges[i].begin(), write_ranges[i].end());
+        }
+
+        bool writes_overlap = false;
+        bool dependent_srcs = false;
+        for (const auto & [tensor, stream] : stream_mapping) {
+            const ggml_tensor * t = tensor->view_src ? tensor->view_src : tensor;
+            const int64_t       t_start = (int64_t) t->data;
+            const int64_t       t_end   = t_start + ggml_nbytes(t);
+
+            // skip tensors that overlap with join_node's buffer
+            if ((t_start <= join_start && join_start < t_end) || (join_start <= t_start && t_start < join_end)) {
+                continue;
+            }
+
+            // check if this buffer's write data overlaps with another stream's
+            std::pair<int64_t, int64_t> data_range = std::make_pair(t_start, t_end);
+            for (int i = 0; i < n_streams; ++i) {
+                if (i == stream - 1) {
+                    continue;
+                }
+                auto it = std::lower_bound(write_ranges[i].begin(), write_ranges[i].end(), data_range);
+
+                if (it != write_ranges[i].end()) {
+                    const std::pair<int64_t, int64_t> & other = *it;
+
+                    // std::lower_bound returns the first element where other >= data_range (lexicographically).
+                    // This guarantees other.first >= data_range.first.
+                    // Therefore, overlap occurs iff other.first < data_range.second
+                    // (i.e., the other range starts before this range ends).
+                    if (other.first < data_range.second) {
+                        GGML_LOG_DEBUG("Writes overlap for %s", tensor->name);
+                        writes_overlap = true;
+                        break;
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+
+            //check if all srcs are either in branch or don't have a branch
+            for (int i = 0; i < GGML_MAX_SRC; ++i) {
+                if (!tensor->src[i]) {
+                    continue;
+                }
+
+                auto it = stream_mapping.find(tensor->src[i]);
+
+                if (it == stream_mapping.end()) {
+                    continue;
+                }
+
+                if (it->second != stream) {
+                    dependent_srcs = true;
+                    break;
+                }
+            }
+
+            if (dependent_srcs || writes_overlap) {
+                break;
+            }
+        }
+
+        return !writes_overlap && !dependent_srcs;
+    }
+
+    ~ggml_cuda_concurrent_event() {
+        if (fork_event != nullptr) {
+            CUDA_CHECK(cudaEventDestroy(fork_event));
+        }
+        for (cudaEvent_t e : join_events) {
+            if (e != nullptr) {
+                CUDA_CHECK(cudaEventDestroy(e));
+            }
+        }
+    }
+};

+            for (auto it = cuda_graphs.begin(); it != cuda_graphs.end(); ) {
+                if (time_now - it->second->last_used_time >= 10'000'000) {
+                    it = cuda_graphs.erase(it);
+                } else {
+                    ++it;

+            }
+        }

+        auto it = cuda_graphs.find(first_node_ptr);
+        if (it == cuda_graphs.end()) {
+            it = cuda_graphs.emplace(first_node_ptr, std::make_unique<ggml_cuda_graph>()).first;
